llm.summary: The files implement a local CLI roadmap tool that stores data under your home directory and does not request secrets or network access, but the SKILL.md and metadata contain multiple mismatches with the shipped script (env var handling, commands, version), so the package is internally inconsistent and warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose (a command-line roadmap/productivity tool) matches the included script: it writes logs and supports add/plan/track/export/status operations and stores data under ~/.local/share/roadmap. However there are small mismatches: SKILL.md lists different top-level commands (e.g., 'run', 'list') and the registry version (1.0.4) does not match the SKILL.md/script version (2.0.0). These are likely packaging sloppiness but worth calling out.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md claims you can set ROADMAP_DIR to change the data directory, but the script does not read ROADMAP_DIR (it hardcodes DATA_DIR from HOME). SKILL.md also advertises commands that don't map one-to-one with the script's dispatch (e.g., 'run' vs 'plan/track/etc.). This mismatch could confuse users or cause unexpected file writes to your home directory.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no network fetches; the skill is instruction-only with a bundled script. That is low-risk from an installation point of view (nothing is downloaded at install time).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials (and the script does not use any credentials). SKILL.md mentions ROADMAP_DIR as configurable via env, but the script ignores it — this inconsistency is non-sensitive but misleading.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill only writes to a per-user data directory (~/.local/share/roadmap). It does not modify other skills or system-wide settings and contains no autonomous network callbacks.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a simple local CLI tool that writes and reads logs in ~/.local/share/roadmap and does not request secrets or perform network calls. However: (1) SKILL.md claims ROADMAP_DIR env support but the script ignores it — expect files to be written to ~/.local/share/roadmap unless you modify the script; (2) the documented commands and version in SKILL.md/registry do not fully match the script, indicating sloppy packaging. Before installing or enabling: review the script contents yourself, run it in a sandbox/container or as a non-privileged user, and confirm the data directory and behavior are acceptable. If you rely on ROADMAP_DIR, ask the author for a corrected release or modify the script to honor it. If you plan to export/share data, note the export implementation does not escape values for JSON output and could produce malformed JSON for inputs containing quotes or newlines.
